events.text: In the training yard behind the village hall your legendary weapon starts to ring against the rack, all on its own, and a voice like a war drum says: "Your footwork is a farmer's." It is the Iron Marshal, the soul of a general who held the river ford till the last boat crossed. It has decided you will do.

choices.text: Ask the Marshal to drill you at the ford

effects.log: It drills you in the shallows till your arms shake, then once more. "Adequate," it says. From the Marshal, that is a medal.

choices.text: Say that plain footwork has fed a family

effects.log: "So did mine," the Marshal says, "until it did not." But it laughs, short and hard, and stays.

events.text: You nick your thumb on your own weapon while mending a fence, and instead of the sting there is warmth and a low humming. A soft voice says, "Oh, forgive me. Let me." The cut closes. The spirit in the blade is called Willow, and it has been fretting over you since the spring planting.

choices.text: Thank Willow, and promise to be careful

effects.log: Willow hums all evening, pleased as a hen. Every hurt you take after that mends a little cleaner.

choices.text: Ask why a gentle soul sleeps in a weapon

effects.log: "Someone has to keep you from swinging it at the wrong people," says Willow. You think about that, off and on, for years.

events.text: At a market-town inn your legendary weapon begins to rattle in its sheath, and a voice cackles: "At last! Somebody worth waking for! Who are we fighting? Is it the innkeeper? Is it the whole street?" It calls itself Stormcrow, and it has been bored since before the town had walls.

effects.log: "A promise!" Stormcrow crows. "I will hold you to it." It does, daily, from the rack above your bed.

choices.text: Tell it to be quiet, you are eating

effects.log: Stormcrow sulks for three days. On the fourth it tells you a joke so good you choke on your dumpling. You are friends.

events.text: You are copying a ledger by lamplight when a dry voice from the weapon on the shelf says, "That column is wrong, you know. I kept the accounts for the first magistrate." It is Old Ink, the soul of a swordsman who kept more books than he broke bones, and it has an opinion on every page in the district.

choices.text: Have Old Ink go over the ledger

effects.log: It corrects it, and the next, and the next, till dawn. Your mind has never been so tired, or so clean.

choices.text: Ask Old Ink about its own last fight

effects.log: It tells you, step by step, and at the end you understand a stance you had only ever copied.

events.text: Your boots are in the hayloft. Your belt is down the well. Your legendary weapon is exactly where you left it, giggling. A tiny voice says, "You took ages to notice me!" The spirit is called Pebble, and it is delighted with itself and with the entire farmyard.

effects.log: Pebble is thrilled that you laughed. Things still go missing, but now they turn up in lucky places.

choices.text: Tell Pebble that partners do not hide boots

effects.log: Pebble thinks about it very seriously and agrees, mostly. The boots stay put. The belt does not.

events.text: At midnight, with the shutters barred against a cold wind, your legendary weapon goes frosty in your hand, and a voice like ice on a pond says, "So you carry me now. You are softer than the last. We will see to that." The spirit names itself Ashen Fang.

choices.text: Tell Ashen Fang you will not be seen to

effects.log: Ashen Fang is silent a long while. "Stubborn," it says at last. "Good. Stubborn lasts." It stays.

choices.text: Ask Ashen Fang what it can teach you

effects.log: It teaches you, coldly and very well. Some of its lessons you decide not to keep. It notices.

events.text: One night your legendary weapon hums on its peg above the hearth, and for a moment a presence looks out of the iron at you: old, proud, not impressed. "Not you," it says. "Not yet." Then the iron is only iron again, and the fire pops.

choices.text: Swear to be worth its waking

effects.log: You say it to the empty kitchen. Nothing answers. The weapon is a little heavier on its peg after that.

choices.text: Shrug; it is a good weapon either way

effects.log: You shrug and bank the fire. It cuts as well as ever. Somewhere in it, something keeps watching.

events.text: At dusk, polishing your legendary weapon on the doorstep, you feel it consider you, and set you down. A cold clear voice that is not quite a voice says, "Come back when you have stopped being afraid of it." The neighbour's dog whines. The weapon sits dull and quiet in your lap.

choices.text: Ask what you are afraid of

effects.log: No answer comes, but you spend the night with the question, and some of the dark in it goes.

choices.text: Hang it back up and go to supper

effects.log: You go to supper. The weapon hangs where it hung. Once or twice that night you look up at it, and it does not look away.
